Appendix A Appendix

Neumann heat semigroup

It is well known that the first eigenvalue of the Neumann Laplacian, defined on its domain

WN2,s(Ω):={f∈W2,s(Ω):∇f⋅ν=0 on ∂Ω},W_{N}^{2,s}(\Omega):=\{f\in W^{2,s}(\Omega):\nabla f\cdot\nu=0\text{ on }\partial\Omega\},

is zero when s=2s=2, and so, the first eigenvalue of −Δ+I-\Delta+I is 11. Moreover, the family {et⁡(Δ−I)}t≥0\{e^{t(\Delta-I)}\}_{t\geq 0}, generated by −Δ+I-\Delta+I, is an analytic semigroup of linear bounded operators on L2​(Ω)L^{2}(\Omega). Thanks to [HW05, Lemma 2.1], there exists λ>0\lambda>0 such that

‖(Δ−I)k​et⁡(Δ−I)​f‖Ls​(Ω)≤C​e−λ​t​t−k​‖f‖Ls​(Ω),t>0,\displaystyle\|(\Delta-I)^{k}e^{t(\Delta-I)}f\|_{L^{s}(\Omega)}\leq Ce^{-\lambda t}t^{-k}\|f\|_{L^{s}(\Omega)},\quad t>0, (A.1)

for all 1<s<∞1<s<\infty. If k=0k=0, we can take λ=C=1\lambda=C=1 as well as s=∞s=\infty, see [Ama84, Theorem 13.4]. On the other hand, it holds for all 1≤p≤q≤∞1\leq p\leq q\leq\infty that

‖et⁡(Δ−I)​f‖Lq​(Ω)≤C​e−t​min⁡(t,1)−N2​(1p−1q)​‖f‖Lp​(Ω),t>0,\displaystyle\|e^{t(\Delta-I)}f\|_{L^{q}(\Omega)}\leq Ce^{-t}\min(t;1)^{-\frac{N}{2}(\frac{1}{p}-\frac{1}{q})}\|f\|_{L^{p}(\Omega)},\quad t>0, (A.2)

see [QS19, Proposition 48.4].

Inequalities for balancing energy functionals

Throughout the paper, we denote

L​log⁡L⁡(Ω):={ϕ∈L1​(Ω)|∫Ωmax⁡(|ϕ|​log⁡|ϕ|; 0)<∞}.\displaystyle L\log L(\Omega):=\left\{\phi\in L^{1}(\Omega)\bigg|\int_{\Omega}\max(|\phi|\log|\phi|;\,0)<\infty\right\}. (A.3)

Proof of Lemma A.1 in the case N=4N=4 can be found in [FS17]. Since we consider 1≤N≤41\leq N\leq 4, we present its proof below for convenience.

Lemma A.1.

Assume f∈L​log⁡L​(Ω)f\in L\log L(\Omega) is a nonnegative function such that ∇f∈L2​(Ω)\nabla\sqrt{f}\in L^{2}(\Omega). Then, for any α>0\alpha>0, there exists a constant Cα>0C_{\alpha}>0 such that

‖f‖LNN−1​(Ω)2≤α⁡(∫Ω(f​log⁡f+e−1))​‖∇f‖L2​(Ω)2+Cα.\displaystyle\|f\|_{L^{\frac{N}{N-1}}(\Omega)}^{2}\leq\alpha\left(\int_{\Omega}(f\log f+e^{-1})\right)\|\nabla\sqrt{f}\|_{L^{2}(\Omega)}^{2}+C_{\alpha}. (A.4)
Proof of Lemma A.1.

For s>1s>1, we define g:=(f−s)+g:=(\sqrt{f}-\sqrt{s})_{+}. By the Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality,

‖g‖L2​NN−1​(Ω)4≤C​‖∇g‖L2​(Ω)2​‖g‖L2​(Ω)2≤C​‖∇f‖L2​(Ω)2​‖g‖L2​(Ω)2,\displaystyle\|g\|_{L^{\frac{2N}{N-1}}(\Omega)}^{4}\leq C\|\nabla g\|_{L^{2}(\Omega)}^{2}\|g\|_{L^{2}(\Omega)}^{2}\leq C\|\nabla\sqrt{f}\|_{L^{2}(\Omega)}^{2}\|g\|_{L^{2}(\Omega)}^{2},

where the latter norm can be estimated as follows

∥g∥L2​(Ω)2≤∥f∥L2(Ω∩{f≥s})2=∫Ω∩{f≥s}f≤1log⁡s∫Ω(flogf+e−1).\displaystyle\|g\|_{L^{2}(\Omega)}^{2}\leq\|\sqrt{f}\|_{L^{2}(\Omega\cap\{f\geq s\})}^{2}=\int_{\Omega\cap\{f\geq s\}}f\leq\frac{1}{\log s}\int_{\Omega}(f\log f+e^{-1}).

Moreover, using the inequality (a+b)p≤2p−1​(ap+bp)(a+b)^{p}\leq 2^{p-1}(a^{p}+b^{p}) for all a,b≥0a,b\geq 0 and p≥1p\geq 1, we have

‖f‖LNN−1​(Ω)2\displaystyle\|f\|_{L^{\frac{N}{N-1}}(\Omega)}^{2} ≤(∫Ω∩{f≥s}((f−s)+s)2​NN−1+∫Ω∩{f<s}(f)2​NN−1)2​N−2N\displaystyle\leq\left(\int_{\Omega\cap\{f\geq s\}}\left((\sqrt{f}-\sqrt{s})+\sqrt{s}\right)^{\frac{2N}{N-1}}+\int_{\Omega\cap\{f<s\}}(\sqrt{f})^{\frac{2N}{N-1}}\right)^{\frac{2N-2}{N}}
≤(2N+1N−1​∫Ω(f−s)+2​NN−1+max⁡(2N+1N−1; 1)​∫Ω(s)2​NN−1)2​N−2N\displaystyle\leq\left(2^{\frac{N+1}{N-1}}\int_{\Omega}(\sqrt{f}-\sqrt{s})_{+}^{\frac{2N}{N-1}}+\max\left(2^{\frac{N+1}{N-1}};\,1\right)\int_{\Omega}(\sqrt{s})^{\frac{2N}{N-1}}\right)^{\frac{2N-2}{N}}
≤8​‖(f−s)+‖L2​NN−1​(Ω)4+2N−2N​max⁡(23​N−2N+2, 1)2​N−2N​|Ω|2​N−2N​s2.\displaystyle\leq 8\|(\sqrt{f}-\sqrt{s})_{+}\|_{L^{\frac{2N}{N-1}}(\Omega)}^{4}+2^{\frac{N-2}{N}}\max\left(2^{\frac{3N-2}{N+2}};\,1\right)^{\frac{2N-2}{N}}|\Omega|^{\frac{2N-2}{N}}s^{2}.

Combining the above estimates gives

‖f‖LNN−1​(Ω)2≤8​Clog⁡s​(∫Ω(f​log⁡f+e−1))​‖∇f‖L2​(Ω)2+2N−2N​max⁡(23​N−2N+2, 1)2​N−2N​|Ω|2​N−2N​s2,\displaystyle\|f\|_{L^{\frac{N}{N-1}}(\Omega)}^{2}\leq\frac{8C}{\log s}\left(\int_{\Omega}(f\log f+e^{-1})\right)\|\nabla\sqrt{f}\|_{L^{2}(\Omega)}^{2}+2^{\frac{N-2}{N}}\max\left(2^{\frac{3N-2}{N+2}};\,1\right)^{\frac{2N-2}{N}}|\Omega|^{\frac{2N-2}{N}}s^{2},

which ends the proof by choosing ss such that 8​C​(log⁡s)−1=α8C(\log s)^{-1}=\alpha. ∎

Lemmas A.2-A.3 below can be respectively found in [FS17, Lemmas 7.1 and 3.5].

Lemma A.2.

Let β>0\beta>0. If f,gf,g are nonnegative functions such that f∈L1​(Ω)∩L​log⁡L⁡(Ω)f\in L^{1}(\Omega)\cap L\log L(\Omega), then

∫Ωf​g≤1β​∫Ωf​log⁡f+‖f‖L1​(Ω)β​log⁡(∫Ωeβ​g)+1e,\displaystyle\int_{\Omega}fg\leq\frac{1}{\beta}\int_{\Omega}f\log f+\frac{\|f\|_{L^{1}(\Omega)}}{\beta}\log\left(\int_{\Omega}e^{\beta g}\right)+\frac{1}{e}, (A.5)

whenever the latter logarithm is finite.

Next, we present two consequences of the Moser-Trudinger and Adam-type inequalities, where the second one is restricted to a radially symmetric setting. Let BRB_{R} be the open ball centred at the origin of a given radius 0<R<∞0<R<\infty, and H𝗋𝖺𝖽2​(BR)H_{\mathsf{rad}}^{2}(B_{R}) be the set of all radially symmetric functions in H2​(BR)H^{2}(B_{R}).

Lemma A.3.

Given β>0\beta>0 and η>0\eta>0.

  • i)

    (A consequence of the Moser-Trudinger inequality) If N=2N=2, then there is Cβ>0C_{\beta}>0 such that

    log⁡(∫Ωeβ​g)≤β28​π​‖∇g‖L2​(Ω)2+β|Ω|​∫Ωg+Cβ,\displaystyle\log\left(\int_{\Omega}e^{\beta g}\right)\leq\frac{\beta^{2}}{8\pi}\|\nabla g\|_{L^{2}(\Omega)}^{2}+\frac{\beta}{|\Omega|}\int_{\Omega}g+C_{\beta}, (A.6)

    for all g∈H1​(Ω)g\in H^{1}(\Omega).

  • ii)

    (A consequence of the Adam-type inequality) If N=4N=4, then there is Cβ,η>0C_{\beta,\eta}>0 such that

    log⁡(∫BReβ​g)≤(β2128​π2+η)​‖(Δ−I)​g‖L2​(BR)2+Cβ,η,\displaystyle\log\left(\int_{B_{R}}e^{\beta g}\right)\leq\left(\frac{\beta^{2}}{128\pi^{2}}+\eta\right)\|(\Delta-I)g\|_{L^{2}(B_{R})}^{2}+C_{\beta,\eta}, (A.7)

    for all g∈H𝗋𝖺𝖽2​(BR)g\in H_{\mathsf{rad}}^{2}(B_{R}).

Linear parabolic equations with slow evolution

For a given small relaxation parameter 0<ε≪10<\varepsilon\ll 1, we consider in general regularity of the solution uεu_{\varepsilon} to the linear parabolic equation

{∂tuε=1ε​(d​Δ​uε−uε+f)in ​Ω×(0,T),∇uε⋅ν=0on ​Γ×(0,T),uε​(0)=u0on ​Ω.\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{lllll}\partial_{t}u_{\varepsilon}=\dfrac{1}{\varepsilon}\left(d\Delta u_{\varepsilon}-u_{\varepsilon}+f\right)&\text{in }\Omega\times(0,T),\\ \nabla u_{\varepsilon}\cdot\nu=0&\text{on }\Gamma\times(0,T),\\ u_{\varepsilon}(0)=u_{0}&\text{on }\Omega.\end{array}\right.

where d>0d>0 is a diffusion coefficient, the functions ff and u0u_{0} are given. We focus on the maximal regularity and local-in-space regularity uniformly in the relaxation parameter ε\varepsilon.

Lemma A.4.

Let 0<ε<10<\varepsilon<1 and uεu_{\varepsilon} be the solution to Problem (A). Assume that u0u_{0} satisfies the compatibility condition ∇u0⋅ν=0\nabla u_{0}\cdot\nu=0 on Γ\Gamma. Then, for any 1<p,q<∞1<p,q<\infty,

supε>0(‖uε‖W2,p​(Ωt))≤(εp)1p​‖u0‖W2,p​(Ω)+Cp​‖f‖Lp​(Ωt),\displaystyle\sup_{\varepsilon>0}\Big(\|u_{\varepsilon}\|_{W^{2,p}(\Omega_{t})}\Big)\leq\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{p}\right)^{\frac{1}{p}}\|u_{0}\|_{W^{2,p}(\Omega)}+C_{p}\|f\|_{L^{p}(\Omega_{t})}, (A.11)

and

supε>0(‖uε‖Lq​((0,T),W2,p​(Ω)))≤Cp,q​(‖u0‖W2,p​(Ω)+‖f‖Lq​((0,T),Lp​(Ω))),\displaystyle\sup_{\varepsilon>0}\Big(\|u_{\varepsilon}\|_{L^{q}((0,T);W^{2,p}(\Omega))}\Big)\leq C_{p,q}\left(\|u_{0}\|_{W^{2,p}(\Omega)}+\|f\|_{L^{q}((0,T);L^{p}(\Omega))}\right), (A.12)

where the constants CpC_{p}, Cp,qC_{p,q} are independent on ε\varepsilon.

Proof.

Estimate (A.11) was proved in [RTY24, Lemma 3.4]. To prove (A.12), we consider the rescaling t′=t/εt^{\prime}=t/\varepsilon and the substitution

u^ε​(x,t′)=uε​(x,t)andf^​(x,t′)=f⁡(x,t),\widehat{u}_{\varepsilon}(x,t^{\prime})=u_{\varepsilon}(x,t)\quad\text{and}\quad\widehat{f}(x,t^{\prime})=f(x,t),

which recasts Problem (A) to the form

{∂t′u^ε=d​Δ​u^ε−u^ε+f^in ​Ω×(0,T/ε),∇u^ε⋅ν=0on ​Γ×(0,T/ε),u^ε​(0)=u0on ​Ω.\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{lllll}\partial_{t^{\prime}}\widehat{u}_{\varepsilon}=d\Delta\widehat{u}_{\varepsilon}-\widehat{u}_{\varepsilon}+\widehat{f}&\text{in }\Omega\times(0,T/\varepsilon),\\ \nabla\widehat{u}_{\varepsilon}\cdot\nu=0&\text{on }\Gamma\times(0,T/\varepsilon),\\ \widehat{u}_{\varepsilon}(0)=u_{0}&\text{on }\Omega.\end{array}\right.

Then, by applying Lp−LqL^{p}-L^{q} maximal regularity, we get

‖Δ​u^ε‖Lq​(0,T/ε,Lp​(Ω))≤Cp,q​(‖u0‖W2,p​(Ω)+‖f^‖Lq​(0,T/ε,Lp​(Ω))),\displaystyle\|\Delta\widehat{u}_{\varepsilon}\|_{L^{q}(0,T/\varepsilon;L^{p}(\Omega))}\leq C_{p,q}\left(\|u_{0}\|_{W^{2,p}(\Omega)}+\|\widehat{f}\|_{L^{q}(0,T/\varepsilon;L^{p}(\Omega))}\right), (A.13)

where the constant Cp,qC_{p,q} is independent on the terminal time TT and the parameter ε\varepsilon. By noticing that ∥φ^∥Lq​(0,T/ε,Lp​(Ω))=ε−1/q∥φ∥Lq​((0,T),Lp​(Ω))\|\widehat{\varphi}\|_{L^{q}(0,T/\varepsilon;L^{p}(\Omega))}=\varepsilon^{-1/q}\|\varphi\|_{L^{q}((0,T);L^{p}(\Omega))} for φ∈{u;f}\varphi\in\{u;f\} as well as ε<1\varepsilon<1, we obtain (A.12). ∎

Lemma A.5.

Let N≥3N\geq 3 and uεu_{\varepsilon} be the solution to Problem (A) for each ε>0\varepsilon>0. Then,

supε>0(ε​∫Ωuε2+∬Ωt(|∇uε|2+uε2))≤∫Ωu02+Cd2​∫0t‖f‖L2​NN+2​(Ω)2,\displaystyle\sup_{\varepsilon>0}\left(\varepsilon\int_{\Omega}u_{\varepsilon}^{2}+\iint_{\Omega_{t}}\left(|\nabla u_{\varepsilon}|^{2}+u_{\varepsilon}^{2}\right)\right)\leq\int_{\Omega}u_{0}^{2}+\frac{C}{d^{2}}\int_{0}^{t}\|f\|_{L^{\frac{2N}{N+2}}(\Omega)}^{2}, (A.14)

for any t∈(0,T)t\in(0,T), provided that the right-hand side exists finitely.

Proof.

Using the Sobolev embedding H1​(Ω)↪L2​N/(N−2)​(Ω)H^{1}(\Omega)\hookrightarrow L^{2N/(N-2)}(\Omega) and the Young inequality, we see

∫Ωfε​uε\displaystyle\int_{\Omega}f_{\varepsilon}u_{\varepsilon} ≤‖f‖L2​NN+2​(Ω)​‖uε‖L2​NN−2​(Ω)≤C​‖f‖L2​NN+2​(Ω)​‖uε‖H1​(Ω)\displaystyle\leq\|f\|_{L^{\frac{2N}{N+2}}(\Omega)}\|u_{\varepsilon}\|_{L^{\frac{2N}{N-2}}(\Omega)}\leq C\|f\|_{L^{\frac{2N}{N+2}}(\Omega)}\|u_{\varepsilon}\|_{H^{1}(\Omega)} (A.15)
≤d2​∫Ω(|∇uε|2+uε2)+Cd​‖f‖L2​NN+2​(Ω)2.\displaystyle\leq\frac{d}{2}\int_{\Omega}\left(|\nabla u_{\varepsilon}|^{2}+u_{\varepsilon}^{2}\right)+\frac{C}{d}\|f\|_{L^{\frac{2N}{N+2}}(\Omega)}^{2}. (A.16)

Therefore, testing this equation by uεu_{\varepsilon}, we get

12​dd​t​∫Ωuε2+dε​∫Ω|∇uε|2+1ε​∫Ωuε2≤d2​ε​∫Ω(|∇uε|2+uε2)+Cd​ε​‖f‖L2​NN+2​(Ω)2,\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega}u_{\varepsilon}^{2}+\frac{d}{\varepsilon}\int_{\Omega}|\nabla u_{\varepsilon}|^{2}+\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\int_{\Omega}u_{\varepsilon}^{2}\leq\frac{d}{2\varepsilon}\int_{\Omega}\left(|\nabla u_{\varepsilon}|^{2}+u_{\varepsilon}^{2}\right)+\frac{C}{d\varepsilon}\|f\|_{L^{\frac{2N}{N+2}}(\Omega)}^{2},

and consequently,

dd​t​∫Ωuε2+dε​∫Ω|∇uε|2+1ε​∫Ωuε2≤Cd​ε​‖f‖L2​NN+2​(Ω)2.\displaystyle\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega}u_{\varepsilon}^{2}+\frac{d}{\varepsilon}\int_{\Omega}|\nabla u_{\varepsilon}|^{2}+\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\int_{\Omega}u_{\varepsilon}^{2}\leq\frac{C}{d\varepsilon}\|f\|_{L^{\frac{2N}{N+2}}(\Omega)}^{2}.

Then, integrating the two sides of the latter inequality over time gives

ε​∫Ωuε2+∬Ωt(|∇uε|2+uε2)≤ε​∫Ωu02+Cd2​∫0t‖f‖L2​NN+2​(Ω)2,\displaystyle\varepsilon\int_{\Omega}u_{\varepsilon}^{2}+\iint_{\Omega_{t}}\left(|\nabla u_{\varepsilon}|^{2}+u_{\varepsilon}^{2}\right)\leq\varepsilon\int_{\Omega}u_{0}^{2}+\frac{C}{d^{2}}\int_{0}^{t}\|f\|_{L^{\frac{2N}{N+2}}(\Omega)}^{2},

and consequently shows estimate (A.14) by noticing that ε≪1\varepsilon\ll 1. ∎

For the sake of convenience, we also present here a linear differential inequality with slow evolution, which can be easily proved.

Lemma A.6.

Given ε>0\varepsilon>0. If a continuous function y:[0,T]→[0,∞)y:[0,T]\to[0,\infty) satisfies that

ε​dd​t​x​(t)+a​x​(t)≤y⁡(t),0≤t≤T,\displaystyle\varepsilon\frac{d}{dt}x(t)+ax(t)\leq y(t),\quad 0\leq t\leq T,

for some a>0a>0, then

x(t)≤x(0)e−at/ε+1ε∫0te−a(t−s)/εy(s)ds,0≤t≤T.\displaystyle x(t)\leq x(0)e^{-at/\varepsilon}+\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\int_{0}^{t}e^{-a(t-s)/\varepsilon}y(s)ds,\quad 0\leq t\leq T.
